submission.natural_language_explanation: Across ordinary text this head is active-weak at most tokens and peaks when the current token predicates on, refers to, or completes an already-established composite nominal: the verb, copula, pronoun, determiner or possessive clitic whose subject or anchor is a multi-token name or a noun given preceding clausal context such as a preamble, a prior clause, or a quoted-speaker setup, and non-initial pieces and intra-word punctuation finishing such names, with most of its attention focused on that one earlier token. The first token of any input, immediate self-repeats of low-information words such as the, he, is and said, and the verb of a clause whose subject is a single-token noun standing clause-initially with no preamble or prior clause stay at floor; replacing the anchor with a different word of the same structural shape leaves the peak unchanged.
